title: Natural Domain and Range of a Rational Fraction
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the function defined by the formula f(t) = \frac{4}{3 - t}.

steps.title: Identify Denominator Singularities
steps.explanation: In any rational function, division by zero is undefined. The denominator 3 - t must not equal zero, which requires t != 3.
steps.why: Division by zero does not represent a valid operation in the real number system.

steps.title: Formulate Domain in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: Since there are no radical restrictions or other algebraic constraints, all real numbers except t = 3 are admissible.
steps.why: Excluding the single singularity t = 3 leaves the union of two open infinite intervals.

steps.title: Analyze the Range by Solving for the Input
steps.explanation: Set y = 4/(3 - t) and solve for t in terms of y. This yields t = 3 - 4/y, which is well-defined for every real number y except y = 0.
steps.why: Expressing the independent variable in terms of the dependent variable exposes any restrictions on the output.

steps.title: State the Range
steps.explanation: A fraction with a non-zero numerator (here 4) can never equal zero. As t approaches 3 from either side, f(t) grows arbitrarily large in positive or negative magnitude, covering all non-zero real numbers.
steps.why: The horizontal asymptote y = 0 is never attained by 4/(3 - t) for any finite real input t.
